title: Total Chlorophyll a Measurements by Spectrophotometer
author: Dr. Steven Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ijpccmn
materials: Collect materials on 0.2 µM polycarbonate membrane filters with gentle filtration Record the volume that is being filtered in L. The volume to be filtered is dependent on the sample in question. Typically, it will range from 25 mLs to 100 mLs. The more productive (eutrophic) the system, the less you will filter. You should avoid adding too much material as this will clog the filter and it will no longer select based on size exclusion.

steps.title: Prepare Samples
steps.instruction: Obtain culture or field samples, ensuring at least duplicate or preferably triplicate samples are processed for chlorophyll extractions.

steps.title: Extract Chlorophyll
steps.instruction: Extract chlorophyll from the sample using 90% acetone.

substeps.instruction: Place the filter containing the sample into a 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Store the sample and acetone in the dark overnight to allow for extraction of Chl a.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Read the standards in a spectrophotometer at three specific absorbance wavelengths.

steps.title: Calculate Chlorophyll Concentration
steps.instruction: Calculate the concentration of Chl a in the extract and the original sample using the provided equations.

substeps.instruction: Calculate mg/L Chl a in the extract: 11.75*(A665-A730)-1.31*(A645-A730).
Calculate total chlorophyll extracted: Chlorophyll in sample (mg/L) * acetone volume.
Calculate concentration in original sample: Total chlorophyll extracted (mg) / volume filtered (L).
